label: D29-pemulihan-store-riwayat
decision: How should the iOS app recover when the local tap-history store (SwiftData, 30-day log) cannot be opened at launch, given that today this failure makes the whole app fall back to the 'storage unavailable' mode with no cards?

candidates.description: On open failure use InMemoryTapHistoryStore for this session and leave the file untouched; the next launch tries again. Persistent history stays unavailable for as long as the file remains unreadable (possibly until reinstall).
On open failure delete the TapHistory directory and retry once; if the retry also fails use InMemoryTapHistoryStore. Old unreadable history is lost; persistence is restored.
Inspect the thrown error; delete and recreate only for corruption or migration errors (SQLite 26/11, model incompatibility); for any other error use InMemoryTapHistoryStore without deleting.

priorities: 1) Opening doors must never depend on the tap-history log: cards and presentation stay available when it fails. 2) FR-30 history should work persistently again after a failure, without reinstalling. 3) Do not destroy history that is still readable. 4) Keep the code small and testable on the host (Swift Testing, temporary directory).
requirements: A tap-history store that cannot be opened never makes cards or presentation unavailable.
After the history file becomes corrupt or unmigratable, history is persisted across launches again without reinstalling the app.
History that can still be read is never deleted.
